newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Four killed in Colombian cement plant blast.
newsitem.headline: Four killed in Colombian cement plant blast.

text.p: At least four people were killed and 16 were seriously injured on Friday when a blast caused red-hot cement to rain down on workers in a factory in central Colombia, authorities said.

Alvaro Ramirez, mayor of the city of Ibague in Tolima province, said the explosion at the Caracolito cement plant on the city's outskirts at about 1:35 p.m. was apparently caused by a malfunction in one of the plant's boilers.
The blast caused cement being heated at extremely high temperatures to spew out of a cauldron and tear through the factory like napalm, burning almost everything in its path, witnesses said.

Spokesmen for Cementos Diamante, owner of the Caracolito plant, said they had no immediate comment. But Guillermo Linares, head of medical services at the local Social Security Institute hospital in Ibague, said four workers were killed in the blast and 16 others were being treated for severe burns covering as much as 80 percent of their bodies.
Four of the 16 were in critical condition with third-degree burns, Linares said.
